verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into his Counter Strike stun after level 6; you win if you punish his Leap Strike cooldown with Death's Grasp pulls before he scales.

brief.thesis: Jax's E (Counter Strike) only dodges basic attacks, not spells, so Mordekaiser's Q (Obliterate) and E (Death's Grasp) go through it clean while autos risk eating the stun. The lane evens out because Jax's R (Relentless Assault) stacks attack speed for free starting at level 6, turning extended auto exchanges in his favor exactly when Morde's early spell-poke advantage fades.

theirWindow.when: After level 6, in extended auto trades
theirWindow.what: Once Jax has R, every third consecutive attack hits harder and his attack speed climbs with no cooldown of its own. Disengage after 2-3 exchanged hits instead of staying in a prolonged duel.

yourWindow.what: Leap Strike is 17s at rank 1, so right after he jumps in he has no gap-closer back out. Pull him with E (Death's Grasp) and commit Q plus autos before he can reset.

start.why: The 49.9% win rate pick across 2041 games; the extra mana and AP let you keep poking with Q and E through Jax's early all-in windows without running dry.

boots.why: 77.7% pick rate at 48.8% win rate; the flat damage reduction on autos directly answers Jax's attack-speed stacking from R once he hits 6.

core.why: Part of the highest-performing path (55.3% win rate, 228 games); the slow on Q and E makes it much harder for Jax to Leap Strike away after a trade.

runes.keystoneWhy: The 53% pick rate page at 49% win rate; stacking Conqueror through repeated Q and E hits in forced trades builds the adaptive force you need to outlast Jax's attack-speed scaling.

summoners.why: 77.1% pick rate at 48.9% win rate; in an even lane, Ignite's early kill pressure during your levels 1-5 edge is what tips individual trades before Jax's level 6 power spike arrives.

playing.title: Trade with spells, not autos
playing.detail: Jax's E (Counter Strike) stance only dodges basic attacks, so Q (Obliterate) and E (Death's Grasp) go through clean. Walking autos into a stance that can stun you is the losing habit to avoid.

playing.title: Bait his Counter Strike before all-in
playing.detail: Counter Strike is 18s at rank 1, dropping to 10s at max rank. Watch for it going on cooldown before you commit your full combo.

playing.title: Punish Leap Strike's long early cooldown
playing.detail: At rank 1, Leap Strike is 17s. The moment Jax uses it to engage, he has no way back out, so pull him deeper with Death's Grasp and finish with Q and autos.

playing.title: Watch for the Empower glow
playing.detail: W (Empower) is up as fast as every 3-7 seconds and makes his next attack or Leap Strike hit nearby enemies for bonus damage. Respect it before standing in range.

playing.title: Disengage once his R stacks after level 6
playing.detail: Relentless Assault has no cooldown and ramps his attack speed every hit, with bonus damage every third strike. Take 2-3 exchanges then back off instead of dueling it out.

playing.title: Consume your shield to heal, don't hoard it
playing.detail: W (Indestructible) is already banking damage from both sides of the trade. Pop it for the heal when you're low rather than saving it defensively.

playing.title: Save R for a decisive mid-game skirmish
playing.detail: Realm of Death drags Jax into another dimension and steals his stats, keeping them if you kill him. Use it once your Rylai's/Riftmaker core is online so the stat steal and sustain swing the fight your way.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample-size figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the ability mechanics and tactical reasoning (when to pull, when to bait, what to punish) are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Jax will slowly regain control over lane as he reaches level 6. Purchase Plated Steelcaps, Bramble Vest, and other items that increase armor before closing in to deal damage.
